FINDING_ID: GPT_R3_FSM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: `select_event()` can return `Event.COMPLETE` from `State.SYNTH` whenever `round_complete=True`, even if `self.max_round_idx == 0`. In that configuration, `transition(Event.COMPLETE)` moves `SYNTH -> ROUND_1`, creating a round state that exceeds the documented maximum iterative round index `(N-1)=0`. This violates the FSM’s own bound and the claim “Terminates in at most N + 2 transitions.” Reachable if `config.max_rounds <= 1`, or more generally whenever the configuration permits no iterative rounds beyond synthesis. No validation in this area prevents such a config.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `config.max_rounds >= 2` in `DynamicManagementConfig.__post_init__` or `RoundProgressionFSM.__post_init__`. Additionally, guard `SYNTH -> ROUND_1` so it is only allowed when `max_round_idx >= 1`; otherwise `select_event()` should emit `MAX` or a dedicated terminal transition from `SYNTH`.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: GPT_R3_FSM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: The documented event priority in `select_event()` says `FAIL_CRITICAL > CONVERGED > DIMINISHED > COMPLETE > MAX`, but the implementation special-cases `round_complete` on the last round to return `Event.MAX` instead of `Event.COMPLETE`. That means the public contract mixes two different semantics: a priority ordering over events, and a state-dependent substitution of one event for another. This is not just wording drift: a caller using `valid_events()` plus the documented priority could conclude that `COMPLETE` remains the completion event everywhere, while `MAX` is separately selectable. In reality, on the terminal round `COMPLETE` is invalid and completion is encoded as `MAX`. The FSM API therefore exposes completion with inconsistent symbols depending on state.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make the contract explicit: either (a) redefine the priority documentation to say “completion maps to COMPLETE except on the final round, where it maps to MAX,” or (b) simplify the API so callers always signal `COMPLETE` and `transition()` internally converts final-round completion into terminal `MAX_ROUNDS`. The second option is cleaner.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: GPT_R3_FSM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.61  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: `transition()` trusts the string format of `current_state` and parses round indices via `int(s.split("_")[1])` in multiple places. Because `current_state` is a mutable public dataclass field, external code can set malformed values such as `"ROUND_x"`, `"ROUND_1_EXTRA"`, or `"SYNTH "` and trigger uncaught parsing failures or invalid behavior in `valid_events()`, `select_event()`, and `transition()`. This area has no internal state invariant enforcement despite presenting a deterministic FSM abstraction.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make FSM state private or expose it as a read-only property backed by an internal enum/index representation, e.g. `{phase: Enum, round_idx: Optional[int]}`. Add invariant checks before parsing, and reject impossible states with a controlled `ValueError`.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: GPT_R3_FSM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.57  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47  
DESCRIPTION: The docstring says the FSM state set is `{BLIND, SYNTH, ROUND_1, ..., ROUND_{N-1}, TERMINAL}` and that `current_round = 0` represents BLIND, but there is no documented or enforced meaning of `current_round` while in `SYNTH` or `TERMINAL`. After `BLIND -> SYNTH`, `current_round` remains `0`; after termination from any round, it remains whatever prior round number happened to be set. This creates an ambiguous API contract for consumers using `current_round` as the authoritative phase index. A manager may incorrectly infer that `SYNTH` is “round 0 complete” or that terminal-from-synthesis occurred at round 0.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Specify and enforce `current_round` semantics per state, e.g. `None` for `BLIND/SYNTH/TERMINAL`, or add a separate `phase` field and reserve `current_round` only for `ROUND_k` states. Update transitions accordingly.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: GPT_R3_FSM_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.49  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.51  
DESCRIPTION: `validate_no_failures()` is incorrect for the `max_rounds == 1` edge case. It performs `BLIND -> SYNTH -> ROUND_1`, then directly calls `Event.MAX`, even though `ROUND_1` is already beyond the documented state set when `N-1 == 0`. Depending on configuration validation elsewhere, this validator can either fail spuriously or pass while validating an impossible chain. Since validators are part of the area’s claimed reduction properties, this weakens confidence in the FSM boundary conditions.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add explicit preconditions for supported `max_rounds` values and branch validator logic for degenerate cases. Better: centralize legal FSM topology construction from config and have validators consume that topology instead of hardcoding transitions.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: GPT_R3_FSM_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.44  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.56  
DESCRIPTION: `valid_events()` reparses `current_state` and recomputes the same event set on every call, and `select_event()` calls `self.valid_events()` repeatedly for membership checks. In normal use this is small, but this FSM is intended as orchestration control and may be queried multiple times per scheduling cycle. More importantly, repeated recomputation against mutable public state opens a tiny TOCTOU-style inconsistency window if outside code mutates `current_state` between checks. This is primarily a robustness/performance smell rather than a major defect.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Cache `valid = set(self.valid_events())` once at the top of `select_event()`, and preferably make state immutable from outside to eliminate recomputation against mutable strings.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: GPT_R3_FSM_X001  
SEVERITY: 0.54  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: [UNVERIFIED cross-component] The FSM termination causes are purely event-driven (`CONVERGED`, `DIMINISHED`, `MAX`, `FAIL_CRITICAL`) with no explicit coupling to detector data freshness. From the surrounding signatures, `ConvergenceDetector`, `DiminishingReturnsDetector`, and `FailureHandler` all maintain round-indexed histories, but this area does not encode any guard that the predicates supplied to `select_event()` were computed for the current round/state. A manager bug could therefore terminate on stale detector outputs from a previous round without the FSM noticing. This is plausible given prior round-index issues elsewhere, but cannot be proven from this scope alone.  
PROPOSED_FIX: In `DynamicManager.process_round()`, carry an explicit round token/version and only call `select_event()` with detector results tagged to `fsm.current_round` (or the just-completed round). Optionally extend `select_event()` to accept `event_round_idx` and validate consistency.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

Definitive stance: the strongest new issues in this area are the unguarded degenerate `max_rounds` topology, the inconsistent completion/MAX contract, and the lack of FSM state invariant protection.
